import itertools
import json

reps = ["Kim", "Mahr", "Parra", "Quinn", "Stuckey", "Tiao", "Udall"]
idx = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(reps)}
zones = [1, 2, 3]

def givens_ok(a):
    K, M, P, Q, S, T, U = (a[idx[n]] for n in reps)
    if not ((P == 1) != (T == 1)):        # exactly one of Parra, Tiao in Zone 1
        return False
    if not ((T == 2) != (U == 2)):        # exactly one of Tiao, Udall in Zone 2
        return False
    if P != Q:                            # Parra and Quinn same zone
        return False
    if S != U:                            # Stuckey and Udall same zone
        return False
    counts = {z: sum(1 for x in a if x == z) for z in zones}
    if not (counts[3] > counts[2]):       # more in Zone 3 than Zone 2
        return False
    return True

def antecedent_ok(a):
    return a[idx["Mahr"]] == a[idx["Stuckey"]]   # Mahr and Stuckey same zone

models = [a for a in itertools.product(zones, repeat=len(reps))
          if givens_ok(a) and antecedent_ok(a)]

options = {
    "A": ("Kim", 2),
    "B": ("Mahr", 1),
    "C": ("Parra", 3),
    "D": ("Stuckey", 2),
    "E": ("Tiao", 1),
}

witnesses = {}
for letter, (rep, zone) in options.items():
    witnesses[letter] = sum(1 for a in models if a[idx[rep]] == zone)

possible = [L for L, w in witnesses.items() if w > 0]

if len(possible) == 1:
    final_answer = possible[0]
else:
    final_answer = "UNSUPPORTED"

evidence = {
    "satisfying_models_with_antecedent": len(models),
    "witness_counts_per_option": witnesses,
    "possible_options": possible,
}

print(json.dumps({"final_answer": final_answer, "evidence": evidence},
                 separators=(",", ":")))
